Text: - Turkish conquest of North India started in about 1000 CE under *Mahmud of Ghazna*
The Formation of Classical Indian Civilization (187 BCE - 320 CE), The Classical Age (320-600 CE), Late Classical Indian Civilization (600-1000 CE)
- In 1000-1200 CE  it was Muslim Turks from Afghanistan, that raided India, creating the Sultanate of Delhi.
- *Qutb-ud-din Aybak* as the first sultan of Delhi in 1206
- Turks established their rule of Delhi in 1206
- Caused by the Mongols who destroyed the Abbasid caliphate in 1258
- Gunpowder warfare was in India before *Babur* but he was good at artillery giving him an advantage at the Battle of Panipat in 1526 where he defeated the Sultan of Delhi
- Mughals from 1526
- Humayun 1530-2556
- Jahangir 1605-1628
- Kandahar in Afghanistan was lost to the Persians in 1622  confining the Mughals to India
- Shah Jahan 1628-1658
- Aurangzeb 1658-1707
- Pakistan and the republic of India were created in 1947
- Ceylon (Shri Lanka) was given independence from Britain in 1948, the Maldives in 1965 and Bangladesh broke away from Pakistan in 1971
- East Pakistan split in 1971 and became Bangladesh
- Western kingdom fell ~90 BCE
- Nepal considered itself the last Hindu kingdom before it became a republic in 2008
- By the 1st century CE  we hear of South Asian kingdoms that adopted Indian culture
- By the end of the 1st century or start of the 2nd  *Kanishka* greatest of the Kushana kings ruled the empire
- In Western India Dynasties of Scythian extraction started in 1st century CE and lasted till the end of the 4th Century
- In the 1st century CE  a clan of the Yuezhi, the Kushanas, established its hegemony over the rest and expanded into India
- In the last decades of the Eastern Kingdom (1st century BCE  )there were invasions from the Scythians and Parthians (called Shakas and Pahlavas by the Indians) from the northwest
- Legend says Buddhism arrived in China in 1st Century CE

- While classical Indian Civilization was forming there were many nomadic invasions from the northwest, growing indigenous kingdoms in the south, and, in the 1st century CE  the Roman trade route with India
- came to an end around 1900 BCE
- By the 14th century there were many mamluk kings
- Eastern kingdom fell ~30 BCE
- By 2nd century BCE   *Demetrius*’s kingdom had split in two
- By the end of the 2nd century CE  *Kanishka*’s line vanished with the start of the Sassanian Empire in 3rd century  Iran

- In 2nd century BCE  Chinese records show that warfare in Central Asia had driven a people called the Yuezhi to the borders of Bactria, from where they expelled the Scythians by the end of the century

- This Tamil courtly literature is called the Sangam literature in reference to anthologies of Tamil poetry compiled by a sangam (a gathering of literary connoisseurs) in the Pandya kingdom of *Madurai* in the 2nd-4th century CE
- The first wave was the Iranian speakers, then in the 5th century  it was the Hunas, probably speaking Turkish (relatives of the Huns)
- As *Gupta* rule recedes eastward in the 6th century  independent kings show up in regions that were previously tribal
- the governors of Bengal still reported to the Guptas until late in the 6th century
- first half of 7th century   *Harsha*, prince of Thaneswar (near Delhi) made an empire from the eastern Punjab to Bengal and Orissa with allies in Kathiawar and Assam
- In the middle of the 8th century  two major powers emerged
- The Chahamanas divided into 8 or 9 branches by 1000
- *Skanda Gupta* (455-470)  son of *Kumara Gupta* takes credit for fighting off the Hunas
- During the rule of *Chandra Gupta II* (376-415)   and his son *Kumara Gupta I* (415-455)  India was prosperous while Central Asians caused trouble everywhere else
- 326 BCE  the Nanda dynasty ruled Magadha which included much of North India to the north of the Indus basin
- They kept the Muslim power to the Indus region where Arabs had reached by 712
- In the 15600s  the Mughals started the largest (pre-European imperialism)  Indian empire
- However the governor *Aurangzeb* put in charge quickly became independent and stated the dynastic line of the *Nizams of Hyderabad* who ruled until the 1940s
- British rule began in the 1760s
- now a non accepted idea, since 1924 when evidence of the Indus Civilization was identified
- In 9th century  a vassal lineage with the name Chola from one of the three ancient Tamil kingdoms founded an empire
- By the end of the 10th century  Rashtrakutas were replaced by the *Chalukyas* who came back and unified the upper Deccan
- Their empire broke up in the 10th Century
- The Palas lost Kanyakubja to their rivals in ~800  and were confined to Bihar and Bengal where they ruled until the end of the 11th century
- They reached their peak in 11th century and lasted into the 13th
- They resumed the conquest of North India by the end of the 12th century
- They ruled until the end of the 12th century  when it broke up into successor states
- in 187 BCE   ~50 years after the death of Ashoka *Pushyamitra Shunga*, who was the brahmin general of the Mauryas took over by a coup d’etat
